tests/unit/test_docker_inputs.py:26-30: the test collects the set of python:3.N versions from FROM lines and unpacks it as exactly one element (a zero-match or multi-version Dockerfile raises ValueError, not a silent pass). It then asserts that version is in the matrix of both ci.yml (job unit) and dependency-audit.yml (job audit), so a bump to 3.15 fails unless both matrices run it. This is stricter than the comment's 'neither', so the guard is at least as strong as claimed. Non-matching FROM forms: if all stages mismatch the unpack fails. If only one stage mismatched, the sibling test at lines 16-20 requires both stages to match the same pinned pattern, which covers 'exactly one Python'. Head Dockerfile has both stages on python:3.14-slim-bookworm@sha256 (docker/Dockerfile:6,31). The matrices are ci.yml:38 ['3.11','3.12','3.13','3.14'] and dependency-audit.yml:21 ['3.11','3.12','3.14'], both containing 3.14 as strings.

tests/unit/test_docker_inputs.py:23-30 extracts the single Dockerfile FROM python:X.Y version and asserts it is in jobs.unit matrix of ci.yml (ci.yml:32,38 matrix 3.11-3.14) and jobs.audit matrix of dependency-audit.yml (lines 14,21 matrix 3.11,3.12,3.14); so the test fails unless the version is in both, matching the doc.
